solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Judge to authorise revision of Times sketch, finally, for comedian

indicators.note: a revision reworks the text, so the letters of TIMES get rearranged

parts.note: to OK something is to authorise it

indicators.note: take only the last letter of sketch

explanation.surface: An editor approves a rewrite of a comic sketch for the Times, commissioned from a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Times, sketch and comedian all sound like the newspaper's own business, which hides that Times is just five letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A jokesmith is someone who crafts jokes, a comedian or gag-writer.

clue.text: Jack and Sally at the fair for an outing

parts.note: J = jack, as on playing cards
Aunt Sally is a fairground game, so the fair's Sally is AUNT

explanation.surface: Jack and Sally have a day out at the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British fairground game in which players throw sticks or balls at a dummy's head; the clue asks what Sally's first name is there.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaunt is a short pleasure trip, an outing.

clue.text: Calm down and continue to bet everything?

definitions.meaning: the idiom telling someone not to lose their temper
literally, go on staking your shirt on a bet, i.e. everything you own

explanation.surface: Advice to a gambler: stay cool and keep going all in.
explanation.walkthrough: To bet your shirt on something is to stake all you have, so keeping your shirt on a horse means leaving everything riding on it; the question mark flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone about to strip off their shirt for a fight is told to stop; the betting sense treats the shirt as your last possession.

clue.text: Watch muscle getting into condition

indicators.note: the muscle gets inside the word for condition

explanation.surface: A trainer keeps an eye on a muscle as it gets into shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Watch looks like a noun, a timepiece, sitting beside a muscle and a condition as if in a gym; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: spectators are the people who watch a match or show.

clue.text: Some — not all — in pub, I admitted, initially showing wakeful state

indicators.note: only some of the word some is used, so drop its last letter
the shortened word sits in the pub
take only the first letter of admitted

explanation.surface: Someone owns up that they have a few drinks, which explains their sleeplessness.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes make 'not all' look like an aside, but it is the instruction to cut SOME short before placing it inside INN.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is the condition of being unable to sleep, a wakeful state.

clue.text: Player kept in shade? Very kind

indicators.note: the player is held inside the shade

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
a man is a player, as a piece in chess or a member of a team

explanation.surface: A cricketer resting in the shade is thanked for a kind gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: Shade suggests shelter from the sun, but it is the colour sense, HUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: humane treatment spares suffering, which is kindness in a strong degree.

clue.text: Review amount raised

explanation.surface: An appeal checks how much money has been collected.
explanation.walkthrough: Amount raised sounds like a fundraising total, which is also a fair reading of SUM UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To sum up is to review the main points briefly.

clue.text: Footwear outrage after Conservative's dismissal

indicators.note: outrage remains after the next step
C is sent away from the word

explanation.surface: A politician's dismissal sparks a row over shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: C for Conservative is the standard abbreviation; with it gone, SCANDAL becomes SANDAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandal is an open shoe, a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Use up in moderation — ask to be extravagant

indicators.note: extravagant once meant wandering beyond bounds, so the letters stray out of order

explanation.surface: Advice to spend sparingly rather than lavishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use up in moderation' reads as one phrase that neatly defines the answer, but the definition stops at 'Use up' and 'in moderation' is the start of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To make inroads into a supply is to start using it up.

clue.text: Shared support from bohemian women in cover of darkness

indicators.note: bohemian and women go inside the cover

parts.note: a pall is a dark covering, as of smoke

explanation.surface: Free-spirited women help one another under cover of night.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'cover of darkness' is so familiar it reads as an idiom; here it means a PALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A party wall is a wall shared by two adjoining buildings, supporting both.

clue.text: Vain American first to enrol in a lower degree

indicators.note: only the first letter of enrol is taken

explanation.surface: A conceited American is the first to sign up for an inferior qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a degree from a college; the wordplay means degree as extent, and 'in a lower degree' simply gives LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain in its older sense of futile, not conceited: an attempt made in vain achieves nothing.

clue.text: Part of order retracted about including current name

indicators.note: about is drawn back, so its letters run backwards
the monk takes the current inside

parts.note: a monk is a member of a religious order
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Part of an order is withdrawn and a current name added.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like editing a document, but order is a religious order and the part of it is a MONK.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang synonym, originally tramps' cant, for what someone is called.

clue.text: Essay subject lacking content? Agree to meet

indicators.note: the word is emptied of its middle, leaving the outside letters

explanation.surface: A student's essay topic turns out to be thin, so tutor and student arrange to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: Essay looks like a noun for a piece of writing, but it is the verb meaning attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: To tryst is to arrange a meeting, usually a lovers' one.

clue.text: Blokes caught with it in 24 hours? It's not true

definitions.note: The definition is a sentence describing untruthfulness; the answer is the noun for it.

indicators.note: caught and it go inside the 24 hours

explanation.surface: Men claim they were caught doing it within a day, and someone calls that a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an exclamation, 'It's not true', standing for the quality of lying.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendacity is untruthfulness, the quality of saying what is not true.

clue.text: Nobleman abandoning cold in principal skiing venue?

indicators.note: the nobleman leaves cold behind, losing C
what is left goes inside principal

explanation.surface: An aristocrat quits the chill of a top ski resort.
explanation.walkthrough: C for cold is the tap abbreviation; COUNT without it is OUNT, which sits inside MAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: skiing needs snowy slopes, so a mountain is one venue for it, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Almost impartial copper collared by bloke in capital style

indicators.note: drop the last letter of the word for impartial
a collar goes round the neck, so the bloke goes round the other pieces

parts.note: JUSt without its last letter; just = impartial
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A nearly fair policeman is arrested by a man in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper and collared paint an arrest scene, but copper is the metal and capital is about letters, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Majuscule is a capital or large letter style of writing.

clue.text: Sports centre abandoned by northern region

indicators.note: northern leaves the word, taking N with it

parts.note: an arena is a sports venue

explanation.surface: A sports centre closes its doors in the north of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Centre invites taking the middle of sports; it is part of the phrase for ARENA.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name a stretch of land or space, as in the local area or region.

clue.text: Islander running narcotics, offloading tons

indicators.note: the narcotics are on the move, so their letters change order
one T is unloaded before the shuffle

explanation.surface: A man from an island smuggles drugs and dumps a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: Running narcotics is a smuggling phrase; running also signals the anagram. T for tons is the standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Corsican comes from the Mediterranean island of Corsica.

clue.text: Role diminished fat, large man

indicators.note: fat is made smaller by losing its last letter

parts.note: L = large, as on clothing sizes
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: A fat actor, slimmed down, plays a large man.
explanation.walkthrough: Fat, large man describes Falstaff himself, which makes it look like the definition; the definition is only Role, and man is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Falstaff is a famous Shakespeare role, the fat knight of Henry IV.

clue.text: Josephine leading quiet banter

indicators.note: to lead is to go in front

parts.note: Josephine cut down to its first two letters, her usual nickname

explanation.surface: Josephine starts some quiet teasing.
explanation.walkthrough: Leading suggests a first letter, but it only places JO ahead of SH.
explanation.definitionFit: To josh is to banter or tease good-humouredly.

clue.text: No lines including expression of farewell? Don't worry about it

indicators.note: the farewell goes inside NO LL

parts.note: NO + LL, L being a line

explanation.surface: An actor with no lines leaves, and someone says it doesn't matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta-ta is a casual British goodbye. The definition is the polite reply to thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Not at all is said to mean don't mention it, no trouble.

clue.text: One piece of legislation I'd overturned for festival

indicators.note: the whole string is turned over, reading backwards

parts.note: a law is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: A new law is overturned in time for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Overturning a law is ordinary political language, which hides that ILAWID is to be read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Hindu celebration of lights held each autumn.

clue.text: Crucial information shunned by western economist

indicators.note: the information avoids W, which drops out

explanation.surface: An economist is ignored by the West despite having vital facts.
explanation.walkthrough: John Maynard Keynes is the British economist behind Keynesian economics.
explanation.definitionFit: Keynes was a leading twentieth-century economist.

clue.text: Sources of some prevalent cold or heat

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so take the first letters

explanation.surface: A weather report on what is behind the current cold or hot spell.
explanation.walkthrough: Cold or heat look like a matched pair of opposites; one is wordplay and the other the definition, joined by or.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat in its culinary sense: the burn of chilli or pepper on the tongue.

clue.text: Vessel losing power carrying American food from Japan

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so the vessel's word goes on without P

explanation.surface: A ship that has lost power brings American food over from Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: The cargo scene makes 'carrying American food' look like one phrase; the definition is only 'food from Japan'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is the Japanese dish of vinegared rice with fish.

clue.text: One dead electric light failed to work

parts.note: d = dead, as on gravestones and in genealogies
an LED is a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: A dead light bulb has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a broken light, and failed to work fits it perfectly; the answer is the lazy sense, not the broken one.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to laze about, and a person who idled did no work; the broken-bulb sense is the decoy.

clue.text: United suffering about limitations of their transport to London?

indicators.note: suffering goes round the next piece

parts.note: U = United, as in football team names

indicators.note: limits are edges, so take the outside letters

explanation.surface: Manchester United fans grumble about the trains they take to London.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain trains towards London are traditionally 'up' trains, whichever direction on the map; the question mark flags that this is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An up-train runs towards the capital, so it is transport to London.

clue.text: French designer adopting extra new medium

indicators.note: the designer takes the letter in

parts.note: Coco Chanel, the French fashion designer
N = new, an extra one next to Chanel's own N

explanation.surface: A French fashion house takes on a new line.
explanation.walkthrough: CHANEL already has one N; 'extra' tells you to add a second.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a means of passing something on, as a TV channel or a spiritualist medium carries messages.

clue.text: One French article with extra heart repelled boredom

indicators.note: pushed back, so the whole reads backwards

parts.note: a second copy of UNE's middle letter

explanation.surface: A Frenchman given a new heart shrugs off his boredom.
explanation.walkthrough: IUNNE read backwards. ENNUI is itself a French word, which fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A French loanword English uses as a plain synonym for weary dissatisfaction.

clue.text: Coolness under pressure if tussling with dragons

indicators.note: the letters wrestle one another out of order

explanation.surface: Staying calm while wrestling dragons.
explanation.walkthrough: Anyone tussling with dragons would need plenty of the answer, so the surface illustrates the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: French for cold blood: staying cool-headed when things get tense.
